_provenance.note: LLM reading of the lens token tables; not a measurement

axes.label: line-ending punctuation / unit words ↔ elements, metals and comparison words
axes.rationale:
The Jacobian lens is the only clear readout: its positive end has element and material words (' aluminium', ' atomic', ' uranium', ' chloride', ' metal') and its negative end has line-ending punctuation ('_
', '…
', '—
'). The real-logit correlation weakly echoes this, with ratio words (' double', ' half', ' twice') positive and unit fragments (' cm', ' cent', ' ang') negative. The logit and tuned lenses agree only with each other, on noise.

axes.label: clause punctuation/newlines ↔ code-identifier fragments
axes.rationale:
On the negative side the Jacobian lens shows sentence and clause endings (',
', '.
', ';
', ' etc', ' whilst'), and the tuned lens has bare punctuation ('-', '?', '.'). The positive side across lenses is code or multilingual noise ('.IContainer', 'mailto', '.Logic'), and the real-logit lists overlap heavily between ends.

axes.label: colon-newline list headers ↔ clearance/spacing words
axes.rationale:
The Jacobian negative end is consistently colon and newline tokens (':
', '：
', ':
'). The positive ends are mostly noise: the logit and tuned lenses share ' clearance', 'SPACE' and ' failed', and the Jacobian adds ' distancing' and ' taller'. The real-logit lists overlap heavily between ends.
